questions.stem: A report loops over a string and tests Character.isLetter; what does it count?

options.text: The number of whitespace characters
The number of digits in the string
The total length of the string
The number of alphabetic characters in the string

questions.explanation: isLetter returns true only for alphabetic characters, so the count is the number of letters. Digits and whitespace are excluded.
questions.hint: The predicate filters letters only.

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: Update min when a smaller value is found
questions.stem: A report updates min inside a loop; complete the comparison condition.

options.text: if(a[i] <= min) min = a[i];
options.misconception: updates on equal, harmless but not needed

options.text: if(a[i] > min) min = a[i];
if(a[i] < min) min = a[i];
if(a[i] != min) min = a[i];

questions.explanation: min should be replaced only when a strictly smaller value appears. Using greater or not-equal would corrupt the minimum.
questions.hint: Replace only on a strictly smaller value.

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: Print a hollow square pattern
questions.stem: A report prints a hollow square; which cells are skipped in the inner loop?

options.text: Every other cell, printing a checkerboard
Border cells, printing stars only inside
No cells, printing a solid square
Interior cells, printing stars only on borders

questions.explanation: A hollow square prints stars on the first and last rows and columns, skipping interior cells. Printing borders only achieves the hollow effect.
questions.hint: Stars go on the edges, spaces inside.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the output of swapped loop bounds
questions.stem: A report swaps outer and inner trip counts from 2x3 to 3x2; what changes?

options.text: Total iterations become five
Total iterations stay six but rows and columns swap
Total iterations become nine
Nothing changes at all

questions.explanation: 2*3 and 3*2 both equal 6, so the total is unchanged, but the grid orientation swaps. The product is commutative.
questions.hint: Multiply the two dimensions both ways.

questions.learningObjective: Predict output when break is inside an inner loop
questions.stem: A report has break inside the inner loop of a nested pair; which loop does it exit?

options.text: Only the outer loop
Both loops at once
Only the inner loop; the outer continues
Neither; break is invalid in nested loops

questions.explanation: break exits only the nearest enclosing loop, which is the inner one. The outer loop proceeds to its next iteration.
questions.hint: Break targets the nearest loop.

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: Choose the right sentinel test placement
questions.stem: A report reads input then tests sentinel; complete the loop structure.

options.text: do{read x;}while(x!=sentinel);
while(x!=sentinel){read x; process;}
while(true){process; if(x==sentinel) break;}
read x; while(x!=sentinel){process; read x;}

questions.explanation: Reading before the loop and again at the end of the body avoids processing the sentinel. Processing before testing would include it.
questions.hint: Read first, then loop, read again at the end.

questions.learningObjective: Classify a number as prime or composite
questions.stem: A report tests 9 for primality; what is the correct classification?

options.text: Prime, because it is odd
Composite, because 3 times 3 equals 9
Prime, because it is greater than 2
Neither, because 9 is not an integer

questions.explanation: 9 is composite because 3 divides it. Being odd or greater than 2 does not imply primality.
questions.hint: Check divisibility by 3.

questions.learningObjective: Repair a variable declared too narrowly
questions.stem: A report fails to compile because total is declared inside the loop but used after; which repair works?

options.text: Cast total to a wider type
Make total a global variable
Move the declaration of total before the loop
Remove the use after the loop

questions.explanation: Moving the declaration before the loop gives it method scope, allowing use after the loop. Global state is unnecessary.
questions.hint: Widen the declaration scope, not the variable type.

questions.stem: A report prints rows 1; 2 3; 3 4 5; what is the first value of row r?

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: Spot an incorrect Fibonacci update order
questions.stem: A report updates a=b; b=a+b; in Fibonacci without a temp; what is wrong?

options.text: The sum should use multiplication
a is overwritten before its old value is used in b
b should be updated first
Nothing is wrong

questions.explanation: After a=b, the old a is lost, so b=a+b uses the new a and produces the wrong term. A temporary preserves the old value.
questions.hint: The old a must survive until b is computed.

questions.learningObjective: Compute GCD of two coprime numbers
questions.stem: A report computes gcd(7,5) with Euclid's loop; what is the result?
questions.explanation: gcd(7,5)=gcd(5,2)=gcd(2,1)=gcd(1,0)=1. Coprime numbers have GCD one.
questions.hint: Run Euclid to termination.

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: Fix a loop that runs one extra time
questions.stem: A report loop while(i<=n) runs one extra time; which corrected condition is right?

options.text: while(i>n), inverting the test
while(i<n+1), keeping the extra run
while(i!=n), stopping at n
options.misconception: skips valid values if gaps exist

options.text: while(i<n), stopping before n

questions.explanation: Changing <= to < stops before n, running exactly n times for 0..n-1. The other conditions either keep or worsen the defect.
questions.hint: Use strict less-than to exclude n.
